title: Poached Apple, Cider and Mustard Pan Sauce
description: Soft apple is pressed into its cider poaching liquid to make a smooth, spoon-coating sauce for pork.

ingredients.name: low-sodium chicken broth
ingredients.note: Use plain meat-and-bone broth without a vegetable seasoning blend.

steps.title: Poach the apple
steps.text: Place {apple}, {cider}, {broth} and {thyme} in the HexClad. Bring to a gentle simmer, then cover and cook over low heat for 8–10 minutes until the apple crushes easily.

steps.title: Smooth the base
steps.text: Lift out the thyme. Press the apple and liquid through a sieve into a heatproof bowl, scraping the pulp from the underside. Return the smooth base to the pan.

steps.title: Thicken the sauce
steps.text: Bring the base to a simmer. Whisk in the freshly stirred slurry and let it bubble for 1 minute, stirring until it coats the back of a spoon.

steps.title: Round out the sauce
steps.text: Swirl {butter} into the finished sauce off heat. Spoon it around lean pork medallions or turkey cutlets.

notes: Make ahead: Poach the apple and sieve the sauce base a day ahead. Refrigerate finished sauce for up to 3 days. Freezer-Friendly Verdict: Yes. Freeze the sauce for up to 2 months; the pureed apple gives it body after thawing. Fridge reheat: Warm in the HexClad over medium-low, stirring with a splash of water or broth if needed. Bring the whole sauce briefly to a rolling boil, then serve. Freezer reheat: Thaw overnight in the refrigerator. Whisk smooth and follow the fridge reheating directions. Option A uses cider and mustard. For gentler Option B, replace the cider with extra broth and omit the mustard. For dairy-free sauce omit the finishing butter.
